summary: A Button that opens a checklist of a table's columns — checked is shown. Pair it with useTableColumns, which also gives resizable headers their handles.
useWhen: a table has more columns than most people need at once, and which ones matter differs by person
a column's content is long — a purpose, a description — and people should be able to give it more room

useInstead.when: some columns matter only on a narrow screen, or only on a wide one
useInstead.why: that is layout, not a choice: stickyFirstColumn and the table's own sideways scroll handle it; a menu asks each person to fix what the page should

useInstead.when: the choice is between a few fixed views of the same data — summary and detail
useInstead.why: one control naming each view says what the choices are; a checklist of twelve columns makes each person build the view

composition.note: Declare the columns once as `TableColumn`s and pass them to `useTableColumns(columns)`. Render the header and body cells of `visibleColumns`, in that order, so a hidden column's cells are not in the table at all; spread `headerProps(key)` onto each header TableCell for its resize handle. Pass the hook's result to `TableColumnsMenu` as `columns`. Give the column that names each row `canHide: false`, and `canResize: true` with `defaultWidth`, `minWidth` and `maxWidth` to the columns whose content is long. To keep a view, store `hidden` and `widths` and restore them with `setHidden` and `setWidths`.

columns.note: the hook's whole result; the menu lists `columns` and changes `hidden`

label.note: the button's text and so the menu's name; "Columns" by default

a11y.role: button that opens a menu of menuitemcheckbox rows
guarantees: each column is a `menuitemcheckbox` that says whether it is shown; Space or a click toggles it, and the menu stays open for the next
a column that cannot be hidden is listed, checked and disabled, and the arrow keys skip it; so is the last column shown
the menu is named by its button, opens on ArrowDown and ArrowUp, and Escape returns focus to the button
a hidden column's cells are not rendered, so a screen reader's column count is the columns on screen
requires: every `TableColumn` has a `label` — its header text, and its row in the menu
notes: Resizing is a drag or the arrow keys on the handle. There is no single-pointer way to set a width other than dragging (WCAG 2.5.7); long content should still be readable at the default width — TruncatedText shows the rest on focus — so a width is a preference, never the only way to read a cell.

antiPatterns.dont: hiding a column with CSS, or rendering empty cells for it
antiPatterns.why: a screen reader still counts and reads the column, and the headers stop matching what is on screen

antiPatterns.dont: letting the naming column be hidden
antiPatterns.why: rows of statuses and dates with nothing to say which row is which are not a table of anything
a handle on every header is a row of drag targets beside every sort button; give one to the columns whose content is long

antiPatterns.dont: clipping a cell's text to fit its width
antiPatterns.do: TruncatedText, which puts the rest in a tooltip on focus
antiPatterns.why: text cut off with no way to read it is lost, whatever width someone chose
